subcomponents.title: Uses scene-kit APIs without bypassing or duplicating them

criteria.rationale: The Talk boundary and the shared Scene both use the kit's public API instead of reimplementing it. Talk.tsx renders the kit's `Presentation` with `steps`, `title` and `initialMode`. steps/index.ts builds `Step<SampleState>` objects with `groupKey`, `Scene` and `payload`, which the kit's Stage consumes. SampleScene.tsx builds every entity from the kit's `Box`, `Label`, `SymbolChip`, `Arrow` and `Frame` inside `SceneLayer`, passing `id` and `appear`. The demo does not duplicate layout, motion or navigation code.
evidence: Talk.tsx: `<Presentation steps={STEPS} title={PRESENTATION_TITLE} initialMode="browse" />` imported from '../../presentation-kit'.
steps/index.ts: `OUTLINE.map(...)` yields `{...beat, groupKey, Scene: SampleScene, payload:{step:index+1}}` typed as `Step<SampleState>`.
SampleScene.tsx: `renderEntity` switch returns the kit's Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow and Frame, and the whole set is wrapped in `<SceneLayer>`.
Stage.tsx reads `step.Scene` and renders it with `payload`, `step`, `stepIndex` and `stepCount`.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Uses stable identities and appropriate grouped-scene architecture

criteria.rationale: Grouping chain: all nine steps come from one `OUTLINE.map` in steps/index.ts, so they share `groupKey: 'how-to-make-a-presentation'` and the same `SampleScene` component. `sceneKey()` turns that into one `group:...:scene:N` key. Stage.tsx uses that key as the `motion.div` key inside `AnimatePresence`, so the scene stays mounted and only `payload` changes. Identity chain: the presentation-owned `ENTITIES` ids in entities.ts are passed as `id` by `renderEntity` in SampleScene.tsx. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Arrow each forward `id` to `layoutId` and carry `layout`, so a persisting entity morphs in place. `ENTITIES.filter(since <= step)` keeps the same ids across steps, and every entity kind is consumed, including arrows.
evidence: steps/index.ts: one shared `groupKey` and `Scene: SampleScene` for all nine OUTLINE-derived steps.
steps.ts `sceneKey`: returns `group:${groupKey}:scene:${id}` when a groupKey is set, so equal keys share one Scene.
Stage.tsx: `<motion.div key={sceneKey(step)}>` wraps `<Scene payload=...>` in `LayoutGroup` and `AnimatePresence`.
entities.ts: `ENTITIES` with stable string ids, e.g. 'you', 'card-1', 'link-1-2', 'conversation' and 'reveal-frame'.
SampleScene.tsx: `common = { id: entity.id, appear: true }` is spread into every kit node.
Box.tsx, Label.tsx, SymbolChip.tsx, Frame.tsx and Arrow.tsx: `layout` plus `layoutId={id}`.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Maintains clear boundaries and scope discipline

criteria.rationale: The presentation's organisation is mostly clear: outline data, entity specs, scene rendering and step wiring live in separate files. The public title contract is consumed: `PRESENTATION_TITLE` goes to `Presentation`, which uses it for `document.title` and `aria-label`. However, entities.ts declares and exports `CARD_STEPS = ['card-1', 'card-2', 'card-3', 'card-4'] as const`. Searching the whole source tree finds no other occurrence of it. The files searched included src/presentations/**, src/presentation-kit/**, src/tests/**, scripts/ and tests/. No import, member access, or `id`, `layoutId` or `key` forwarding uses it. It is a dead presentation-owned constant that implies a contract nothing consumes, which this criterion's guidance treats as a fail.
evidence: entities.ts line 23 declares `export const CARD_STEPS = [...] as const`.
A repo-wide search for `CARD_STEPS` returned only that declaration line.
SampleScene.tsx imports only `ENTITIES` and `EntitySpec` from '../entities'.
Card ids are generated inside `card()` as `card-${slot+1}`, independently of CARD_STEPS.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: Active state is marked in kit chrome and styled by presentation-owned CSS. Footer progress dots and Toc entries set `aria-current='step'` together with the stable hook `data-presentation-active` on the active item only. styles.css gives `[data-presentation-progress-dot][data-presentation-active]` and `[data-presentation-toc-entry][data-presentation-active]` distinct accent colours, glow, bold weight and background. Attribution.tsx is a project-local anchor whose label and href default from the local constants.ts, with no external package or embed. styles.css styles `[data-presentation-attribution]` with muted colour, font, size and underline. The kit itself carries only structural inline styles (flex, position) and no colours, fonts, borders or theme tokens. The only colour reference in the kit is `currentColor` in Arrow.

subcomponents.title: Entity transitions and persistent grouped scenes

criteria.rationale: Every primitive (Box, Label, Frame, SymbolChip, Arrow) is a motion.div with `layout` and `layoutId={id}` and a layout transition of LAYOUT_T with EASE. An entity with the same id therefore animates in place from its old rect, size, label and emphasis to the new one. The wiring test checks that one DOM node persists while its geometry, label and emphasis change.

criteria.rationale: Stage uses AnimatePresence in the default sync mode, not mode="wait". Each scene wrapper is position:absolute, so the outgoing scene is out of layout flow and both scenes are mounted together. Both sit inside one LayoutGroup. A same-id primitive in the next scene's different sceneKey therefore shares its layoutId with the exiting copy and morphs. The primitives apply no entrance hiding by default: initial and animate are only set when appear is passed. The appear delay is on the opacity animate transition only, while layout has its own LAYOUT_T transition.

subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: useFitScale measures the stage element's own bounding rect, on resize and via ResizeObserver. computeFitScale takes one scale = min((w-2*insetX)/880, (h-2*insetY)/380, maxScale), floored at MIN_SCALE. Stage applies that single value as transform scale(s) to a fixed 880×380 canvas centered in the stage, which has overflow hidden. At 1280×720 (browse) the stage is roughly 1100 px wide, so width gives about 1.2; the height of roughly 500 px gives about 1.25, so the scale is about 1.2 and the canvas is about 1060×460, within the stage. At 390×844 in browse mode the Toc is hidden, the stage is 390 px wide, and the scale is (390-48)/880 ≈ 0.39, giving a canvas about 342 px wide. This is above MIN_SCALE, so the floor is not reached. The fit is computed from the stage's own box, not the window, so it accounts for the rendered chrome.
evidence: fit.ts computeFitScale: one scale for both axes, using the mode's insets and maxScale
useFitScale.ts: getBoundingClientRect of the viewport ref plus a resize listener and ResizeObserver

motion-wiring.test.tsx 'stage geometry': scale = 952/880 at 1000 wide, 452/880 after a resize to 500, 968/880 in present mode, with constant canvas dimensions
judging basis: consensus-pass

votes.rationale: The Talk boundary and the shared Scene both use the kit's public API instead of reimplementing it. Talk.tsx renders the kit's `Presentation` with `steps`, `title` and `initialMode`. steps/index.ts builds `Step<SampleState>` objects with `groupKey`, `Scene` and `payload`, which the kit's Stage consumes. SampleScene.tsx builds every entity from the kit's `Box`, `Label`, `SymbolChip`, `Arrow` and `Frame` inside `SceneLayer`, passing `id` and `appear`. The demo does not duplicate layout, motion or navigation code.
evidence: Talk.tsx: `<Presentation steps={STEPS} title={PRESENTATION_TITLE} initialMode="browse" />` imported from '../../presentation-kit'.
steps/index.ts: `OUTLINE.map(...)` yields `{...beat, groupKey, Scene: SampleScene, payload:{step:index+1}}` typed as `Step<SampleState>`.
SampleScene.tsx: `renderEntity` switch returns the kit's Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow and Frame, and the whole set is wrapped in `<SceneLayer>`.
Stage.tsx reads `step.Scene` and renders it with `payload`, `step`, `stepIndex` and `stepCount`.

votes.rationale: Talk.tsx passes STEPS, PRESENTATION_TITLE and initialMode to the kit's Presentation instead of building its own navigation or stage. SampleScene.tsx draws every entity with the kit's Box, Label, SymbolChip, Arrow and Frame inside SceneLayer. It passes id, at, className, emphasis and appear to them, and it does not implement any motion of its own. STEPS is typed as Step<SampleState>[] with Scene and payload. The kit's Stage renders step.Scene with payload, step, stepIndex and stepCount. The demo keeps no duplicate navigation, layout or animation logic.
evidence: Talk.tsx: <Presentation steps={STEPS} title={PRESENTATION_TITLE} initialMode="browse" />

votes.rationale: useFitScale measures the stage element's own bounding rect, on resize and via ResizeObserver. computeFitScale takes one scale = min((w-2*insetX)/880, (h-2*insetY)/380, maxScale), floored at MIN_SCALE. Stage applies that single value as transform scale(s) to a fixed 880×380 canvas centered in the stage, which has overflow hidden. At 1280×720 (browse) the stage is roughly 1100 px wide, so width gives about 1.2; the height of roughly 500 px gives about 1.25, so the scale is about 1.2 and the canvas is about 1060×460, within the stage. At 390×844 in browse mode the Toc is hidden, the stage is 390 px wide, and the scale is (390-48)/880 ≈ 0.39, giving a canvas about 342 px wide. This is above MIN_SCALE, so the floor is not reached. The fit is computed from the stage's own box, not the window, so it accounts for the rendered chrome.

votes.rationale: The port is ephemeral, but freePort closes the reservation before the child binds it. Readiness is taken from HTTP polling of that port, not from the child's own announcement. The only ownership check is isAlive (!exited), sampled once per loop iteration before each fetch. It is not raced against the child's exit. If something else answers on the port after the reservation is released, fetch can return ok before the child's exit is observed, and verification would run against a server it does not own. This matches the guidance's fail case, which is liveness sampled before each poll. Neither accepted mechanism is present.

votes.rationale: Stalled transitions are handled correctly. waitForStepIndex compares the data-step-index string to String(want) and throws VerifyFailure with the step. The integration files are quoted in full. None calls waitForTimeout, a sleep or Playwright directly. Each one runs `npm run verify` or `npm run inspect` through run() in helpers.mjs, which awaits the child's 'close' event before resolving. Its only setTimeout is a SIGKILL watchdog, not a wait for state. The browser waits come from the scripts these tests run, and they poll observable state. verify presses ArrowRight, then waitForStepIndex polls data-step-index with page.waitForFunction and a timeout before it reads the title, caption or era. It also waits for the [data-step-count] selector before reading the count. In inspect, goTo presses ArrowRight and polls data-step-index with waitForFunction before the settle wait and the capture. inspect also waits for [data-step-count] before reading the count. Judge A and Judge B said pass, and the quoted material bears out their reasons. Judge C said fail because INT-002 runs inspect with --settle 2000 and inspect's wait uses page.waitForTimeout. That observation is accurate but does not decide the requirement. The requirement is broken only when a test sleeps for a fixed time instead of waiting for state. In captureSteps, goTo(index) runs before wait(settleMs), and goTo in inspect-presentation.mjs already blocks on waitForFunction until data-step-index equals the target. The settle interval is an extra pause after a state-based wait, so it does not stand in for one. verify's waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS) likewise runs only after waitForStepIndex and the assertions. The guidance also says longer fixed settle delays are not scored. The 20ms setTimeout in src/tests/scripts/inspect.test.mjs is a fake wait callback in a jsdom unit test of captureSteps' ordering, and no browser is involved.

scene-kit.rationale: Stage wraps the keyed scene motion.div in LayoutGroup > AnimatePresence in the default sync mode, not 'wait'. For ungrouped steps the key is `step:${id}`, so the outgoing and incoming wrappers are both mounted. Both are position:absolute, so the outgoing one is out of flow, and both sit in one LayoutGroup. Primitives set no initial opacity unless `appear` is set. When it is set, the 0.6s delay is on the opacity animation only, and the layout transition has no delay. A persisting primitive without `appear` therefore stays visible and morphs between the two scenes.

scene-kit.rationale: The source supports the pass. Continuing entities use `transition={{ layout: { duration: LAYOUT_T, ease: EASE } }}` with LAYOUT_T = 0.5 and no delay, so their layout motion starts immediately. A newcomer's entry comes from `useEnterMotion`. With `appear` set, it returns `initial: {opacity: 0}` (or `false` when instant) and `animate.transition.delay = LAYOUT_T + ENTER_DELAY = 0.6`. That delay sits inside the opacity animate transition only, not in the layout transition, so it does not postpone the continuing layout motion. The entry therefore starts 0.1s after the 0.5s layout move ends, which meets the guidance that the delay be at least the layout duration and apply only to the newcomer's entry. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Arrow each call `useEnterMotion(appear)` and spread `{...enter}` onto their motion.div. `SampleScene.renderEntity` passes `appear: true` to all five kinds declared in `EntitySpec` (box, label, chip, arrow, frame). Every entity the sample gives an identity is rendered through these primitives, so none appears without entry motion. A continuing entity keeps its DOM node, so `initial` is not replayed. `motion-wiring.test.tsx` also checks the delay value, the `>= LAYOUT_T` bound, and that continuing entities keep their node and add no `initial`.

scene-kit.rationale: computeFitScale returns one scalar, the minimum of the width ratio, the height ratio and maxScale. Stage applies it as scale(s) on both axes to the fixed 880×380 canvas, so the internal composition does not reflow. useFitScale measures the stage element's own bounding box, the area the stage actually occupies between the header and footer. It re-measures on window resize, via ResizeObserver, and on mode change. Because the fit comes from that measured area, the scaled canvas stays within it. At 390 wide the stage is at most 390px wide, so the scale is at most (390-48)/880 ≈ 0.39 in browse, giving a canvas about 342px wide. At 1280×720 the width ratio is bounded by the stage width minus the 24px insets, and the height ratio by the stage height minus the 12px insets. The 0.2 floor is not reached at either reference viewport.

votes.rationale: The port is ephemeral, but freePort closes the reservation before the child binds it. Readiness is taken from HTTP polling of that port, not from the child's own announcement. The only ownership check is isAlive (!exited), sampled once per loop iteration before each fetch. It is not raced against the child's exit. If something else answers on the port after the reservation is released, fetch can return ok before the child's exit is observed, and verification would run against a server it does not own. This matches the guidance's fail case, which is liveness sampled before each poll. Neither accepted mechanism is present.

votes.rationale: Stalled transitions are handled correctly. waitForStepIndex compares the data-step-index string to String(want) and throws VerifyFailure with the step. The e2e stall test asserts the failing step. The step count is not handled safely, though. verify.mjs reads `const count = Number(await page.getAttribute('[data-step-count]','data-step-count'))`. waitForSelector only checks that the attribute exists, not that it is numeric. The `count !== expected.length` check runs only for the canonical sample, where expected is non-null. For any other registered presentation expected is null. An empty, non-numeric or zero data-step-count then becomes 0 or NaN, the `for (index < count)` loop runs zero times, and the presentation passes with no steps rendered. The guidance names this case (an unreadable step count steps through no steps and still passes), so the criterion is not met.
